A meeting of the Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) was held on September 10, 2013, to discuss this application.

recommendation.text: The committee voted favorably for approval of Anoro Ellipta 62.5/25 mcg once daily for airflow obstruction in COPD: 13-0 that there was substantial evidence of efficacy, 10-3 that safety had been adequately demonstrated, and 11-2 on approvability.

quote.quote: the results were in favor of approval for airflow obstruction in COPD (11 yes, 2 no, 0 abstain)

linkages.concern: The committee raised that the cardiovascular safety database was limited — few cardiovascular events, few patients with cardiovascular risk factors, and patients withdrawn for ECG/Holter abnormalities — and some members wanted more safety data, suggesting a postmarketing outcome trial, particularly in sicker COPD patients with cardiovascular risks.
linkages.change: FDA concluded a dedicated postmarketing controlled randomized cardiovascular safety trial (505(o)(3) PMR) was not necessary and imposed none (Post-marketing Study Commitments: None); instead the product label was made to include information on the cardiovascular imbalances identified in the clinical development program.

concern_quote.quote: The Committee expressed some concerns with safety assessment in the program, noting the small number of cardiovascular safety events in the program, the limited number of patients with cardiovascular risks factors from the studies, and withdrawal of patients from the studies due to abnormalities on ECGs and on 24-hour Holter monitoring.

change_quote.quote: A dedicated post-marketing controlled randomized safety trial (under the provision of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, Section 505(o)(3)) is not necessary to further explore the cardiovascular safety of Anoro Ellipta.

summary: A Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) meeting was held on September 10, 2013, and voted in favor of Anoro Ellipta (UMEC/VI 62.5/25 mcg once daily) for airflow obstruction in COPD (efficacy 13-0, safety 10-3, approvability 11-2). The committee's main reservation was the limited cardiovascular safety data and generalizability to higher-CV-risk patients, with some members suggesting a postmarketing outcome trial. The review team (SumR and CDTL) explicitly declined a dedicated 505(o)(3) postmarketing cardiovascular trial and imposed no PMR/PMC, instead describing the identified cardiovascular imbalances in the product label; the drug was approved as proposed, so the AdComm's safety suggestions did not produce a required study or a labeling restriction beyond the existing class warnings.
